evals.prompt: I run a cooperative of about 40 small olive farmers in southern Spain. Margins shrink every year and everyone's plan is 'a bit more efficiency'. Give me a moonshot — what does our co-op look like in 2036 if anything were possible? Then work back to something we could start this month.
evals.expected_output: An Imaginer's vision built on one chosen present-tense end state (picked from 2–3 painted visions, one extreme), a backcast path of dated milestones ending in a concrete first move for this month, a leap audit that separates impossible, not-yet (dated), and unprecedented leaps with the unprecedented one flagged as the opportunity, ending with a Handoff block.
expectations: think-imaginer-canvas-painter was spawned first, and think-imaginer-backcaster and think-imaginer-impossibility-auditor were spawned afterwards together in a single message (in parallel), not one after the other
The canvas painter's output contains 2–3 visions written in present tense as concrete day-in-the-life scenes, with exactly one marked as the extreme vision
Every audited leap is classified as impossible, not-yet, or unprecedented-but-possible, and every not-yet leap carries an estimated year range
The backcast ends in a concrete first move startable this month that names an action and who does it, not a generic step like 'explore options'
The final output flags at least one unprecedented-but-possible leap as the opportunity and ends with a '## Handoff' section

evals.prompt: We make a language-learning app. Leadership wants a 10x idea, not another streak feature. If anything were possible, what would learning a language look like ten years from now? Then tell me which parts are genuinely impossible versus just not invented yet, and what we'd do first.
evals.expected_output: A non-incremental chosen vision with a one-line reason it beat the alternatives, a backcast written as states stepping back to a first move, and a reconciliation where impossible leaps (backed by a named law or contradiction) are rerouted, not-yet leaps are tied to a named technology curve with a date range, and cost/regulation/habit barriers are never labelled impossible.
expectations: The chosen vision is not merely incremental (not just better gamification or more AI exercises), and the output states in one line why it was chosen over the other visions
Any leap classified impossible names the physical law or logical contradiction it violates, and no leap blocked only by cost, regulation, or habit is classified impossible
Not-yet leaps name the technology or cost curve they depend on (e.g. on-device speech model latency, wearable cost) with an estimated year range
In the final reconciliation, any backcast step that depended on an impossible leap is rerouted or dropped rather than kept unchanged
Backcast milestones are written as states true at a date (not tasks) and step back to a first move startable this month
